toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The August drop was almost entirely a cooling failure, not the housekeeping contractor or the kiosks. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August because the part wasn't in stock. Rooms ran at 26.5-29 C. Floors 6-8 fell from 8.6 to 7.4, driven by room comfort (8.4 to 6.1). Their scores were 6.8 for 5-20 August checkouts, then recovered to 8.4 and 8.6 once the chiller was fixed. Floors 1-5 stayed within normal variation (8.6 to 8.5). Cleanliness, inspection pass rates, check-in scores, kiosk use and queue times are all flat. The survey method didn't change. 56 of 74 negative comments were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Complaints about room temperature went from 1 to 24.

Recommendations: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Don't serve notice on Orrin and don't pull the kiosks. Don't exclude the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. The guests affected already received an apology and a half-night credit, so any further return-stay offer is optional.

The 6% rate rise may have added a little to the value-score dip on floors 1-5. The evidence can't separate it from the usual August dip. Keep watching it and don't reverse the rise yet. I'm fairly confident in the main conclusion.
